stories.title: CPSC Recalls Two Products Over Button Battery Danger — TIER 1

x_posts.text:

research.facts:
CPSC Button Battery Recalls — JINHEZO + OKK Trading
**Confidence: HIGH** (CPSC.gov official, WRNJ Radio confirmed)
**JINHEZO Mini Waterproof LED Tea Lights:**
- Recalled: August 20, 2026
- Hazard: Button batteries can be accessed easily by children — poses serious ingestion risk, including death
- Violation: Mandatory consumer product safety standard for button cell/coin batteries
research.sources:
- Source: CPSC.gov, WRNJ Radio
**OKK Trading Easter LED Headbands:**
- Recalled for same hazard: button batteries not properly secured
- Risk of serious injury or death from battery ingestion
- Violation: Mandatory toy safety standards
- Source: CPSC.gov
**Context for article:**
- CPSC also announced recalls of infant sleepsuits, children's pajamas, hair serum, and toy building sets in this same batch
- Button batteries remain one of CPSC's top child safety concerns — a swallowed battery can burn through esophageal tissue within 2 hours
- Parents should check CPSC.gov for remedy (refund or return info)
- These are SEPARATE from Aug 20-21 baby lounger recalls already covered

research.facts:
D49 BOCES Dissolution + D11 Free Supplies
**Confidence: HIGH** (district websites, Springs Daily)
**D49 — BOCES Dissolution:**
- D49 Board voted August 17 to dissolve ERBOCES (Education ReImagined BOCES)
- August 19: Colorado State Board of Education affirmed D49 will continue serving students in BOCES-authorized online schools
- New D49 Student Success Center will serve as hub for specialized learning
- Preschool expansion and Base49 moving to former Falcon Elementary building
- D49 is currently in week 3+ of school (started Aug 3-4)
**D11 — Free School Supply Kits:**
- D11 partnering with Edukit to deliver free, grade-specific school supply kits
- More than 14,000 K-8 students will receive kits
- D11 started Aug 12; currently in week 2
- Contact: d11.org
**Context:**
- D20: Stagger start Aug 17-18; currently in week 1 (K/6th/9th started Aug 17, all others Aug 18)
- D49 ~23,000 students; D11 ~25,000 students; D20 ~28,000 students
**Sources:** D49.org, D11.org, Springs Daily (Aug 20, 2026)

research.facts:
AAP Survey — Teens Using AI Chatbots for Mental Health
**Confidence: MEDIUM** (AAP News confirmed, specific study parameters from search summary)
- **Survey:** AAP survey of 1,000+ adolescents and young adults ages 12-21
- **Finding:** 1 in 5 (nearly 20%) had asked an AI chatbot (e.g., ChatGPT) for mental health advice
- **Published:** AAP News, August 2026
- **Context:** Study done alongside pediatrics research; AAP urging parents to have conversations about AI use for personal/health matters
- **Also from AAP August 2026:** Moderate screen time associated with faster concussion recovery in pediatric patients (screen time study using wearable cameras)
- **Verification note:** The 1 in 5 / ~20% figure is MEDIUM confidence — from search summary. Mark as MEDIUM pending verification.
**Sources:** AAP News, AAP Publications (August 2026)
